courthouses.name: Criminal Courthouse
courthouses.hours: Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m., including the noon hour. Drop box for same-day filings/payments until 5:00 p.m.
courthouses.note: Criminal Division (felony and misdemeanor, incl. in-custody arraignments in Dept. 1) and Traffic Division (First Floor, (707) 299-1160). Departments per Criminal Division page as of 2026-10-13 — assignments rotate.

departments.label: Department 1
departments.type: Master calendar — motions, prelims, arraignments, in-custody arraignments, readiness conferences, jury assignments, PC 1001.36 mental health diversion

departments.label: Department 3
departments.type: Misdemeanor arraignments, settlement conferences, review/sentencing, motions, Drug Court, financial evaluations, Prop 36, misdemeanor DEJ/PC 1001.36 hearings

departments.label: Department 4
departments.type: Trials assigned from Dept. 1; settlement conferences (Thursdays 8:30 a.m.)

departments.label: Department 5
departments.type: Trials assigned from Dept. 1; Mental Health Court; mental health diversion review

courthouses.name: Historic Courthouse
courthouses.note: Civil, family and probate (clerk (707) 299-1130); court administration. The county PD 'Locations' page lists the physical address as 810 Coombs Street with 825 Brown Street as mailing address. Also the mailing address for the Juvenile Hall Courthouse.

courthouses.name: Juvenile Hall Courthouse
courthouses.note: Juvenile delinquency (602) calendars and detention hearings Mon & Wed 1:30 p.m. Juvenile filing clerk (707) 299-1291. No mail accepted here — send to 825 Brown St.

legal_aid.name: Napa County DA — Expungement Clinic (online)
legal_aid.serves: People convicted of a crime in Napa County
legal_aid.what: Free online portal to check eligibility and submit expungement forms (CR-180, CR-181, CR-131) by email; DA pays associated court costs; Probation, DA and Court review; expect about 90 days. The page refers questions to a private attorney or the Public Defender (707) 253-4442. Run by the prosecutor's office.

jails.name: Napa County Department of Corrections (Napa County Jail)
jails.phone_note: Main Corrections line; also for bail-bond info and to verify visiting hours. Deposits by phone: 888-277-2535.
jails.note: Run by the Napa County Department of Corrections (not the Sheriff); houses pre-sentenced and sentenced people. Visits: two 30-minute in-person visits per week by housing unit (sign up 30 min before; 8:00–10:30 a.m. and 1:30–4:30 p.m.), free video visits in the lobby (6 stations, book 24h ahead) or paid remote via Smartinmate.com. Deposits: Smartinmate.com, phone, or lobby kiosk; commissary packages via MyCarePack. Mail goes to the PO box in Seminole, FL listed on the FAQ. court_ids: Criminal Courthouse is the county's only adult criminal courthouse — nearest, not confirmed as transport destination.
jails.todo: County page does not explicitly say it houses both men and women ('both' inferred as the only adult jail) — confirm.

jails.name: Napa County Juvenile Hall (Juvenile Justice Center)
jails.phone_note: Juvenile Probation / Juvenile Justice Center line. County FAQ directs visiting questions to (707) 253-4431.
jails.note: Run by Probation. Delinquency detention hearings are held at the Juvenile Hall Courthouse (2350 Old Sonoma Rd) per the court's Juvenile page. Visits: two one-hour visits per week by parents/legal guardians/grandparents approved by the probation officer (county FAQ, seen via search).

bail.note: CA Department of Insurance 'Check a License' — look up a bail agent's license status by name or number. Napa Corrections: a list of licensed bail bond companies is posted at the jail's public entrances and in a Bail Bond List PDF on napacounty.gov/315/Bail-Bonds; call (707) 253-4401. Booking, In Custody and Release reports: services.countyofnapa.org/cjnetweb/Public/. Cash-bail payment method/location at the jail not published on the pages loaded.
